mission: Own process and agent lifecycle state while remaining unable to invoke models, tools or secrets.

operations.notes: Release-aware start remains separately represented by start_release.
Rollback and upgrade use a new process generation and current revocation state.

runtimeTopology: A supervisor process owns generation fencing, launch, health, drain, stop, restart, upgrade and rollback. It starts one Agentd process per enrolled Agent identity and does not own user-task terminality.
physicalState: FleetRegistry and release/signed-intent records are the durable owner surfaces; runtime handles, watchdog state and bounded event buffers are process-local projections. The writer identity is the supervisor generation and registry compare-and-transition fence.
linearization: A lifecycle mutation linearizes at the durable registry or signed-intent transition before process-side acknowledgement. Readiness is published only for the current process and lifecycle generation.
recovery: Startup validates configuration and durable state, recovers signed intents, fences stale processes, and refuses readiness on ambiguous mutation state. Rollback drains and reconciles before loading a compatible predecessor into a new generation.
security: Control methods require exact Agent identity, generation and authorization paths. Stale callbacks, unresolved leases, changed release identity and secret/model/tool access are denied.
capacity: Managed instances <=256 per configured supervisor profile; health batches <=256; restart budgets and watchdog deadlines are explicit configuration. CI verifies bounded buffers and no unbounded retry path.
terminalObserver: The process driver and current-generation health probe may establish process terminality. User-task, provider, Matrix, browser and tool outcomes remain with their effect owners.
externalEvidenceGaps: deployed binary/configuration identity and target-host watchdog measurements
independent operator acceptance of restart, upgrade and rollback behavior
